articles.title: Cyclone Murasu tracker: Where is the storm?
articles.description: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu was located over the west-central Bay of Bengal, around 180 km northeast of Chennai, at 8:30 am IST on Monday, November 2, after moving west-northwestwards at 22 kmph over the previous six hours, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The cyclone is expected to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, from 11:30 pm on Monday to 4 am on Tuesday, November 3, with wind speeds of 100–110 kmph and gusts reaching 120 kmph.At the time of the latest observation, Murasu was centred near latitude 14.1°N and longitude 81.4°E. It was approximately 160 km east-southeast of Nellore, 180 km east-southeast of Kavali, 210 km southeast of Ongole and 240 km south of Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh.The weather department has forecast strong winds and heavy rainfall along the cyclone's projected path. Southern districts of Odisha are also likely to receive heavy rainfall on November 2 and 3, while disaster response teams have been placed on standby in vulnerable areas.Also Read: Weather today, November 2: IMD warns of heavy rain in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu; Delhi-NCR's AQI becomes 'severe'; check latest IMD update and AQI levels— Indiametdept (@Indiametdept) Cyclone Murasu tracker: Where is the storm now?As of 8:30 am on November 2, Murasu was positioned over the west-central Bay of Bengal near 14.1°N latitude and 81.4°E longitude. The severe cyclonic storm had travelled west-northwestwards at 22 kmph during the preceding six hours.Its latest position placed it around 180 km northeast of Chennai and 160 km east-southeast of Nellore. Other locations in Andhra Pradesh near the storm's position included Kavali, Ongole and Machilipatnam, located approximately 180 km east-southeast, 210 km southeast and 240 km south of the cyclone, respectively.The IMD expects the system to continue moving northwestwards towards the south Andhra Pradesh coastline before making landfall as a severe cyclonic storm.Cyclone Murasu tracker: Andhra Pradesh landfall expected between November 2 and 3The IMD has forecast that Murasu will cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole. The landfall window is expected to begin around 11:30 pm on November 2 and continue until approximately 4 am on November 3.The cyclone is expected to bring sustained winds of 100–110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph during the coastal crossing. The forecast places areas along the southern Andhra Pradesh coastline in the path of the severe weather system.Cyclone Murasu tracker: Heavy rainfall in Odisha, NDRF and ODRAF on standbyThe IMD has forecast rainfall of 7–20 cm in southern Odisha districts on November 2 and 3 under the influence of Murasu. Wind speeds in the state could reach 50–60 kmph, with gusts of up to 70 kmph on November 3.National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) personnel have been kept on standby in vulnerable areas. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea from November 2 to 4.In Ganjam district, officials were directed to stock essential supplies and shift residents of high-risk areas to safer shelters by Sunday night, November 1, as part of the preparedness measures.
